Named custom keywords define standalone declarations through keyword Name(signature) [agent=profile] $"prompt", with standalone Name key=value applications and named required compile-time arguments. behavior_boundary.given: Given extensions preserve named/inline trait property/rule contributions and named trait reuse, while named custom keyword definitions introduce new standalone Given statements with targets, arguments and implicit semantics beyond existing Can expressibility. Expose relevant schemas, inputs, outputs, lifecycle, reads and dependencies through typed owner-visible contracts; no anonymous inline keyword definition or prompted keyword application.
behavior_boundary.when: Expose effects and lifecycle entry points where needed and integrate with canonical execution and owning authority. The frozen implementation contract supplies Codex-selected explicit signatures, standalone named arguments and extensible owner-versioned producer bindings; implementation remains unqualified. These entry points integrate with ordinary Can scenarios/handlers and workerd; ordinary When implementations are not generation targets and prompt literals are invalid as do bodies.
behavior_boundary.authority: Generated behavior must expose required authority and use normal owner admission; preserve permissions, version, transaction, exact value, replay and evaluation semantics without hidden storage or privilege bypass.
behavior_boundary.conflicts: Do not silently change explicit author declarations or shared language defaults. Diagnose unresolved/conflicting meaning or definitions before acceptance.
behavior_boundary.expressibility: Human steering requires new local Given keywords with behavior existing .can cannot express. Implement the missing typed extension and runtime integration seams to support it; those gaps do not exclude the requirement or make it an optional broader extension. Current Can checks do not typecheck arbitrary JavaScript.
behavior_boundary.qualification: Can checks cover supported declarations. Generated JS needs interface checking plus relevant actual-workerd behavior checks; neither preflight nor an LLM judgement proves prose correspondence, permissions or sandboxing.

runtime_target.producer: The build-time coding agent produces implementation content and submits it through the custom MCP server against server-issued logical targets; it cannot create output files. The host validates and writes isolated candidates/provenance/metadata for existing acceptance controls. Existing compiler-emitted JS remains the path for ordinary supported Can constructs. Normal When runtime output is deterministically compiler-emitted from ordinary Can bodies, distinct from stochastic generated keyword artifacts.
runtime_target.packaging: Persist accepted generated module bytes and effective generator identity; bundle those modules through the existing portable Worker artifact path rather than evaluating a prompt or generating code on requests.
runtime_target.apis: Use only APIs and dependencies supported by the selected workerd configuration. Do not assume a module that imports or runs under Node also functions in workerd.
runtime_target.execution: Integrate through a defined Can interface/effects boundary so canonical admission, declared grants, transaction commit, failure/replay and exact value representations remain owned by the existing runtime. Generated code must not silently establish separate direct-storage authority.
runtime_target.qualification: Syntax/import preflight plus direct loading and relevant behavior checks in the actual workerd host. Type/interface checking must be designed for generated JS; current Can checks do not establish arbitrary JS correctness or isolation.
runtime_target.status: Target accepted as a human requirement; no generated JS module or new extension registration exists.

generator_output_submission.status: Human-required custom MCP output-submission boundary accepted; generation engine/server/adapters unimplemented.
generator_output_submission.input: The host supplies captured generation context plus server-issued allowed logical output targets. These targets describe admitted artifacts, not filesystem paths chosen by the generator.
generator_output_submission.submission: Build-time generator agents submit structured CSS, JavaScript and other generated code/content to the custom MCP server against those allowed logical targets. They must not create their own output files or supply filesystem destinations.
generator_output_submission.host_ownership: The host validates each submission and controls correct placement, writing isolated candidate files and their provenance/required metadata. Existing validation, leases, current-input/byte/fence checks and acceptance controls govern promotion; submission alone does not accept output.
generator_output_submission.enforcement: Adapters must enforce a read-only/no-write generator environment for protected project, current-output and candidate-output files, with generic write tools and filesystem shell writes disabled for those locations. MCP alone does not isolate filesystem access, and a prompt-only promise is insufficient. Diagnose unsupported runner MCP or enforceable no-write capabilities before launching generation; do not fall back to direct generator file writes. Native CLI session/cache housekeeping may be separately isolated and is not generated application output.
generator_output_submission.lifetime: Private bounded Node tooling session; no new package or persistent daemon. Selected tools: generation_context for immutable context/handles/roles and generation_submit for batches of {target, role, content}; UTF-8 text and checked encoded assets. Transport remains adapter-specific and protected no-write enforcement gates launch.
generator_output_submission.job_grouping: Selected D6 v1: Given preparation precedes dependent frontend consumers; jobs group by compatible effective complete recipe and every frontend job receives whole-Then context plus all style/view intents/use contracts. All required full-retry outputs validate and accept together under one run journal. Incomplete/failed/conflicting sets preserve every current group; recovery restores the whole old set before commit or finishes the whole new set after commit. Selective refinement retains its declared scope. One CLI job may make many model/tool calls.
generator_output_submission.authoring_agent: The user-facing coding agent authoring .can remains permitted to inspect and directly edit primary generated files with existing participating edit leases. It is distinct from the launched build-time generator whose output must pass through MCP.
